reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices quarterly report_January 2024 - March 2024

description.narrative: The program implemented a range of interventions over the reporting period aimed at enhancing youth participation in civic engagement and governance. Key among them was Community Agenda Setting forum activity, which provided a safe space for young people to collectively determine their priorities and aspirations for their communities, established engagement platforms between youth and duty bearers, through sports-based forums and dialogue sessions. These platforms successfully surfaced specific civic and governance challenges faced by the youth, accompanied by actionable recommendations. To amplify awareness and accountability, the program also leveraged social media—running weekly educational posts and creating a social media accountability board to expose poor service delivery and promote transparency. These efforts were supported by sustained advocacy follow-up initiatives. The program noted several challenges in maintaining consistency among county-based civic champions and online champions. These issues were largely attributed to limited capacity and, in some cases, poor attitudes among the youth towards sustained engagement while reliance on individual champions proved unsustainable due to natural youth transitions, which affected continuity in implementing agreed advocacy strategies.
